allow.why: the loop over standard input of the compiled model harness/v2/lean_differential.py runs; no theorem is about it

theorems.name: BlazeGraph.Ledger.fnv1a_from_returns
theorems.says: With more fuel than bytes, the functional model of blaze_graph::ledger::fnv1a_from returns FNV-1a's fold of the seed over the bytes.

theorems.name: blaze_graph.ledger.fnv1a_from.spec.proof
theorems.says: The statement blaze generates from fnv1a_from's ensures holds of its model: it does not panic, and of no bytes it returns its seed.

theorems.name: Blaze.Mir.step_deterministic
theorems.says: A state has one next outcome: the semantics of MIR is deterministic.

theorems.name: Blaze.Mir.run_mono
theorems.says: A run that ends (a value, a panic or undefined behaviour) ends the same with any more fuel.

theorems.name: Blaze.Mir.run_agree
theorems.says: Two runs of one state that both end give the same outcome, whatever their fuel.

theorems.name: Blaze.Mir.State.read_write_other
theorems.says: The frame lemma: a write at a place leaves the read of every place in another slot as it was.

theorems.name: BlazeGraph.LedgerMir.fnv1a_from_model_agrees
theorems.says: The functional model of fnv1a_from and the semantics of its MIR body give the same outcome, for every seed and slice, with 4 * len + 4 steps or more.

theorems.name: BlazeGraph.LedgerMir.fnv1a_from_any_fuel
theorems.says: With any fuel, the MIR of fnv1a_from is out of fuel or returns the fold: it never panics and has no undefined behaviour.

theorems.name: BlazeAgrees.arith.add_one.agrees
theorems.says: The model of arith::add_one and the semantics of its MIR give the same outcome, the value or the overflow panic, for every argument.

theorems.name: BlazeAgrees.early.clamp.agrees
theorems.says: The model of early::clamp and the semantics of its MIR give the same value on both branches, for every argument.

theorems.name: BlazeAgrees.loops.count.agrees
theorems.says: The model of loops::count and the semantics of its MIR give the same value, for every argument, by the loop lemma run_loop.

theorems.name: Blaze.Mir.run_mapBlocks
theorems.says: A rewrite that leaves each block's meaning as it was from every state preserves every run, with the same fuel.

theorems.name: Blaze.Mir.Sim.run
theorems.says: A lockstep simulation through a map on states, under an invariant it keeps, gives equal runs for every fuel.

theorems.name: Blaze.Mir.Opt.removeStorageMarkers_correct
theorems.says: The program without storage markers runs as the program does, for every fuel and state.

theorems.name: Blaze.Mir.Opt.simplifyConstCondition_correct
theorems.says: A switchInt or an assert on a constant made a goto runs as before, for every fuel and state.

theorems.name: Blaze.Mir.Opt.removeNops_correct
theorems.says: The program without nops runs as the program does, for every fuel and state.

theorems.name: Blaze.Mir.Opt.constFold_correct
theorems.says: A binary, checked or unary operation or a cast on constants replaced by its value runs as before; one that panics is left.

theorems.name: Blaze.Mir.Opt.validate_sound
theorems.says: The normal-form validator is sound: a pair of programs it accepts runs alike for every fuel and state.

theorems.name: Blaze.Mir.execStmt_ctl
theorems.says: A statement leaves control as it was: which function each frame runs, the block it is at, and the block its caller goes on at.

theorems.name: Blaze.Mir.execStmt_rename
theorems.says: A statement commutes with a renumbering of blocks: from the renamed state it gives the renamed state.

theorems.name: Blaze.Mir.step_rename
theorems.says: One step of a renumbered program from the renamed state is the renamed step of the program, at every block the renumbering keeps.

theorems.name: Blaze.Mir.Renumbers.sim_total
theorems.says: A renumbering that keeps every block is a lockstep simulation, with no invariant.

theorems.name: Blaze.Mir.step_reaches
theorems.says: The reachability invariant (control is at a live block and returns to live blocks) is kept by every step, when the live blocks are closed under jumps.

theorems.name: Blaze.Mir.Renumbers.sim_live
theorems.says: A renumbering that keeps only a closed set of live blocks is a lockstep simulation on the states the reachability invariant holds of.

theorems.name: Blaze.Mir.Opt.permuteBlocks_correct
theorems.says: A checked permutation of each function's blocks runs as the program does, for every fuel and every state.

theorems.name: Blaze.Mir.Opt.permuteBlocks_call
theorems.says: A checked permutation of blocks gives every call the same outcome.

theorems.name: Blaze.Mir.Opt.removeDeadBlocks_correct
theorems.says: Dead-block removal, when its check passes, runs as the program does from every state the reachability invariant holds of.

theorems.name: Blaze.Mir.Opt.removeDeadBlocks_call
theorems.says: Dead-block removal, when its check passes, gives every call the same outcome.

theorems.name: Blaze.Mir.Stutter.run_target
theorems.says: Under a stuttering simulation with bound K, a target run of n steps that ends is the source's run of K * n steps.

theorems.name: Blaze.Mir.Stutter.run_source
theorems.says: Under a stuttering simulation, a source run of n steps that ends is the target's run of n steps.

theorems.name: Blaze.Mir.Opt.threadGotos_target
theorems.says: A run of the goto-threaded program that ends in n steps is the program's run of 2 * n steps.

theorems.name: Blaze.Mir.Opt.threadGotos_source
theorems.says: A run of the program that ends in n steps is the goto-threaded program's run of n steps.

theorems.name: Blaze.Mir.Opt.threadGotos_call_source
theorems.says: A call that ends in n steps gives the same outcome in the goto-threaded program.

theorems.name: Blaze.Mir.Opt.threadGotos_call_target
theorems.says: A call of the goto-threaded program that ends in n steps gives the same outcome in the program with 2 * n steps.

theorems.name: BlazeDiff.diff_correct
theorems.says: The meaning of diff c x e is the derivative of the meaning of e in variable x, wherever every node is inside its rule's domain.

theorems.name: BlazeDiff.gradient_correct
theorems.says: Each entry of the gradient is the partial derivative in its variable.

theorems.name: BlazeDiff.jacobian_correct
theorems.says: Each entry of the Jacobian is the partial derivative of its root in its variable.

theorems.name: BlazeDiff.hessian_entry_correct
theorems.says: Differentiating a derivative again gives the second partial derivative, where the first derivative is inside the rules' domains.

theorems.name: BlazeDiff.abs_tangent_at_kink
theorems.says: At 0 the generated tangent of abs is the argument's tangent times the choice.

theorems.name: BlazeDiff.abs_choice_is_subgradient
theorems.says: A choice in [-1, 1] is a subgradient of the absolute value at 0.

theorems.name: BlazeDiff.min_tangent_at_tie
theorems.says: At a tie the generated tangent of min is c * t0 + (1 - c) * t1.

theorems.name: BlazeDiff.max_tangent_at_tie
theorems.says: At a tie the generated tangent of max is c * t0 + (1 - c) * t1.

theorems.name: BlazeDiff.max_choice_is_subgradient
theorems.says: A choice in [0, 1] is a subgradient of max at a tie.

theorems.name: BlazeDiff.min_choice_is_supergradient
theorems.says: A choice in [0, 1] is a supergradient of min at a tie.

theorems.name: BlazeDiff.sqrt_tangent_at_kink
theorems.says: At 0 the generated tangent of sqrt is the choice times the argument's tangent (a convention: there is no subgradient).

theorems.name: BlazeDiff.select_tangent
theorems.says: The generated tangent of select is its taken arm's tangent.

theorems.name: BlazeDiff.rewrites_sound
theorems.says: Every fast_math rewrite of the simplifier is an identity over the reals under its stated condition.
